chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the expiation of the vow, so he said: 'The expiation of the vow is the expiation of the oath. And whoever vows an offering (hadyan), upon him is a camel which he should collar, mark, and stop with at Arafat. And whoever vows a 'Juzur' (young camel), he may slaughter it wherever he desires.'

key_terms.بِعَرَفَةَ: At Arafat (the site of Hajj standing)
key_terms.جَزُوراً: A young camel (specifically one that has entered its fourth year)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking or fulfilling a vow in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle that the expiation for a vow (nadhr) mirrors that of an oath (yamin), reflecting the juristic view that a vow carries similar binding weight. It provides specific practical details for sacrificial vows, distinguishing between the ritual presentation of a camel at Arafat and the discretionary slaughter of a juzur, thereby illustrating the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding the fulfillment of devotional commitments.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Hafs Bin Giyas, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked himasws about an expiation of the vow. So heasws said: ‘An expiation of the vow is an expiation of the oath. So the one who vows of a an offering, so upon him is a camel, he should collar it, and mark it, and pause with it at Arafaat; and the one who vows a ‘Juzour’, so he can slaughter it wherever he so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud from Hafs ibn Ghiyath who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the expiation because of a vow and commitment.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Kaffarah (expiation) for a vow and commitment is like the expiation because of an oath. If one makes a vow and commitment to offer an animal for sacrifice he must find a camel, he must mark and collar it and stay with it in ‘Arafah. If one makes a vow and commitment to offer a Jazur, (a certain kind of camel) then he can slaughter by manner of Nahr (slaughtering from the upper part of the chest) wherever he wants.’”
